title: Account-aware aggregation & lightweight scoping template for Sales/CS enterprise asks
creator: Ava Moreno
description: A compact, account-aware process and template to aggregate enterprise feature asks from Sales and Customer Success, produce an initial scope estimate, and surface consolidation opportunities across accounts. Goal: reduce duplicate scoping work, accelerate prioritization for high-impact asks, and produce a single one-page scoping artifact that engineers and solutions engineering can act on. This ticket delivers: 1) a standardized ticket template to be used by Solutions Engineering and AEs; 2) a cadence and thresholds for automated consolidation (by feature surface, technical area, and cost/latency impact); 3) a lightweight estimation rubric (effort, risk, infra impact); and 4) routing rules for urgent/legal/SLA-affecting requests.
acceptance_criteria: Template adopted by Sales/CS onboarding docs and shipped to Confluence: one-page template with fields to collect problem, current workaround, customer priority, and KPI impact.
Automation rule implemented in the intake tracker to flag duplicate asks matching same feature keywords and same technical owners within 48 hours.
Triage rubric validated on a sample of 30 historical enterprise asks and shows >= 70% agreement with previous PM prioritization decisions.
Playbook includes escalation path for requests that require Private/Dedicated changes or security review; path tested with Solutions Eng on two live cases.
Pilot run completed for three accounts (one early-stage startup, one mid-market, one enterprise) and resulting consolidated scoping artifacts reviewed by ENG and SE teams.
Owners and SLAs for follow-up defined (PM response within 3 business days; technical spike estimate within 10 business days when prioritized).
triage_rubric: Technical scope: UI-only=1, API/Model change=2, Infra/Private=3 (weight 0.2)
Composite score >=3.0 => escalates to PM backlog review; >=4.0 => candidate for dedicated engineering spike
aggregation_process: Weekly automated aggregation run groups incoming requests by canonical feature tags, affected component (runtime, console, API, Private), and impacted customers. For groups with >=3 distinct accounts or a single account with high KPI impact score, assign a consolidation owner (Solutions Eng or PM) to produce a consolidated scoping artifact. Manual consolidation allowed for urgent customer escalations. Aggregation results pushed to #pm-enterprise-intake Slack channel and to Confluence summary page.
sample_ticket_template: Customer context: account size, region, product tier, contacts
Problem statement: current limitation and customer-perceived risk
Business impact: MRR/ARR/churn/SLAs affected (quantify when possible)
Technical area: runtime | console | dedicated | private | API | SDK
Attachments: audit logs, screenshots, customer email thread, compliance docs
Initial triage scores: customer_tier, kpi_impact, technical_scope, effort_estimate
Suggested owner for consolidation: Solutions Eng / PM / None
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Publish template and triage rubric to Confluence; run a dry aggregation on past 90 days of tickets; collect feedback from 6 SEs/AEs.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement simple automation in intake tracker to tag and group similar requests; pilot weekly aggregation cadence with three accounts.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Iterate template based on pilot; add routing rules for Private/Dedicated and security reviews; create dashboard for consolidated asks.
Phase 4 (ongoing): Handoff to PM Ops for maintenance; quarterly review for thresholds and rubric calibration.
notes_and_discussions: 2025-02-02: PM sync — decided to bias toward consolidation when 3+ accounts request same surface area to reduce duplicate engineering spikes.
2025-02-07: SE feedback — add an explicit field for 'compatibility with existing model variants / quantization' for requests touching runtime.
2025-02-11: ENG input — infra-impact classification should trigger security_review_required when 'Private' or 'on-prem' is selected.
2025-02-15: Trade-off discussed: strict consolidation reduces context for custom enterprise asks; mitigation: allow account-specific extension notes and preserve original tickets as children.
